name: LMZ22005TZX_NOPB
title: LMZ22005: 5 A step-down power module with inductor inside, 6 V to 20 V in, 0.8 V to 6 V out
summary: A synchronous buck converter built as a module: controller, both MOSFETs and a shielded 3.3 µH inductor sit in one 7-lead TO-PMOD package with a single exposed pad, so a working supply needs only two external resistors and three external capacitors, the output bank totalling at least 200 µF. It runs from 6 V to 20 V, regulates 0.8 V to 6 V from a 0.796 V reference, and delivers up to 5 A (30 W at most). Control is emulated peak current mode with internal compensation, free-running near 812 kHz and lockable to a clock from 650 kHz to 950 kHz. A precision enable with programmable hysteresis, adjustable soft-start or tracking, current limit, output overvoltage and thermal protection are built in, and it starts cleanly into a prebiased output.
key_figures: up to 5 A; 30 W maximum total output power
812 kHz typ free-running; sync 650 to 950 kHz

notes: TZ ships in tubes of 45, TZE on reels of 250 and TZX on reels of 500; each .A code has the same packing as the code it extends.
Extra marking for logo, lot trace code or environmental category may appear beside the part marking.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 6 V to 20 V nominal. The module holds only a little input capacitance; external capacitance from this pin to the exposed pad (PGND) is needed.

pins.name: SYNC
pins.function: Clock input for frequency locking: a CMOS-level square wave between 650 kHz and 950 kHz sets the PWM frequency. Tie to ground when unused; the free-running frequency is then 812 kHz typical.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Precision enable comparator input, rising threshold 1.279 V typical. After the module turns on, a 20 µA internal source switches on at this pin so a series resistor can set hysteresis.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground and the reference for all quoted voltages. Must be tied to EP/PGND outside the package.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input, regulating at 0.796 V; it also feeds the overvoltage and short-circuit comparators. The output-setting divider connects from VOUT to this pin and to AGND.

pins.name: SS/TRK
pins.function: Soft-start and tracking input. A capacitor to ground lengthens the 1.6 ms internal soft-start; a resistor divider from a higher-priority rail makes the output track that rail.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Output, taken from the internal inductor. The output capacitor connects between this pin and the exposed pad.

pins.name: PGND
pins.function: Exposed pad: power ground for the power stage and the main heat path out of the package. Not joined to AGND (pin 4) inside; the two must be connected on the board.

notes: The exposed pad carries PGND and has no lead number.

circuits.title: Typical application, 3.3 V at 5 A
circuits.description: A 7 V to 20 V input stepped down to 3.3 V at up to 5 A. Two 10 µF and two 0.047 µF ceramics decouple VIN at the module, with an optional 150 µF aluminium bulk capacitor. RENT and RENB divide the Enable input to set a 5.46 V rising undervoltage threshold; RENH between the divider and EN adds hysteresis, and the optional 5.1 V zener holds the divider node within the EN rating. RFBT and RFBB set 3.3 V from the 0.796 V reference, with an optional 23.7 Ω resistor in series with RFBT at the output. CSS of 0.47 µF gives about 7.5 ms of soft-start. The output bank is a 220 µF polymer capacitor, an optional 100 µF ceramic and two 0.047 µF ceramics. SYNC is brought out to a clock input and held to ground through the optional 1.5 kΩ resistor.
notes: CIN2,3, CIN1,5 and CO1,6 are each two capacitors in parallel.
The bill of materials adds CFF, 180 pF ±10% C0G, 50 V, 0805, a feed-forward capacitor placed beside RFBT and RFBB at FB.

circuits.title: Simplified application
circuits.description: The minimum circuit: a 22 µF input capacitor, a 220 µF output capacitor, a 0.47 µF soft-start capacitor and the RFBT/RFBB divider that sets the output. SYNC, AGND and PGND go to ground, so the module free-runs, and EN is driven from an external enable line.

operation.text: Emulated peak current-mode control with internal compensation. The valley of the inductor current is sampled during the off-time and used as the starting DC level for the next cycle, with an added ramp; this cuts the minimum on-time without the blanking a true peak-current loop needs, which suits large step-down ratios at narrow duty cycle. The loop regulates FB against an internal 0.8 V reference.

SYNC accepts a clock from 650 kHz to 950 kHz; the input switches at about 1.4 V. The clock should swing about twice that threshold, so driving it from 3.3 V logic through about 1.5 kΩ of source resistance is the suggested way. Unused, SYNC goes to ground directly or through 1.5 kΩ or less. A steady logic high at SYNC means zero PWM frequency and the module stops switching.
When FB rises above 0.86 V, the error amplifier output is pulled toward ground and the output drops.

Two limits act. The low-side limit watches the synchronous MOSFET current during the off-time; above 5.4 A typical it blocks the next switching cycle until the current falls below the limit, which usually halves the switching frequency. The DC current limit depends on duty cycle. The high-side limit, 7 A typical, turns the top MOSFET off at once for the rest of the cycle, and the output voltage falls.

At about 165°C junction the module goes into a low-power standby: the main MOSFET stays off, the output falls and the soft-start capacitor is discharged. Below about 150°C (15°C hysteresis) SS is released and the output ramps back up. Full output current at high input voltage may need extra derating at high temperature.

The module starts correctly into an output that is already partly charged, as happens on boards with several rails and leakage paths between them. With a 1.5 V prebias, the output stays there until the soft-start ramp catches up, then rises to 3.3 V at the rate set by CSS.

At light load the converter runs in discontinuous conduction; above the critical load it runs in continuous conduction, where the inductor current never reaches zero during the off-time. In DCM the average inductor current still equals IOUT and output ripple usually rises. At VIN = 12 V and VO = 3.3 V the module runs in CCM at 3 A and in DCM at 0.3 A. An efficiency or dissipation line marked * has cycle skipping at light load, with slightly higher output ripple.

In order: choose the minimum operating VIN with the enable divider, set VO with the feedback divider, choose CO, choose CIN, work out module dissipation, then lay out the board for the needed thermal performance.

A 2 MΩ resistor inside the module pulls EN up to VIN, so left open the module is always enabled and the internal UVLO turns it on at about 4.3 V rising. EN can be driven directly by logic or a supervisor, or divided from VIN (or from an earlier rail when sequencing) to set a precise input turn-on voltage against the 1.279 V threshold. Once on, 21 µA flows out of EN; RENH in series with EN sets extra hysteresis and can be zero. The 5.1 V zener at the divider midpoint lets the threshold be set for a wide input range without exceeding the EN rating; it is not needed when the EN voltage cannot exceed its maximum.
A divider from VOUT to ground with its midpoint on FB sets the output. For the 3.3 V typical application RFBT is 3.32 kΩ and RFBB 1.07 kΩ.

After the UVLO conditions are met, an internal circuit ramps SS/TRK for a 1.6 ms soft-start, so CSS can be left off when that is fast enough; a capacitor on SS/TRK makes the ramp longer and reduces inrush. 0.47 µF is the suggested starting value. When SS climbs past 0.796 V the 50 µA source turns off, the output now regulating. SS is discharged to ground by an internal sink when EN goes low, on thermal shutdown, and on internal VCC UVLO (about 4.3 V at VIN).

A resistor divider from a master rail (often 3.3 V) to SS/TRK makes this output rise with the master, with a difference during ramp-up typically under 0.15 V. The output must be lower than the master, and the divider values are chosen low enough that the internal 50 µA source has little effect; usually the tracking divider ratio equals the feedback divider ratio. The slave soft-start must be shorter than the master, which holds because the tracking divider takes the place of CSS. Tracking works only during the master power-up; above 0.8 V on SS/TRK the input is no longer active and the 50 µA source is off. Example: a 3.3 V master through Rtkt = 226 Ω over Rtkb = 107 Ω to SS/TRK, with a 2.5 V output set by Rfbt = 2.26 kΩ and Rfbb = 1.07 kΩ.

No output capacitance is inside the module. At least 200 µF is needed for stability with the internal compensation, and this requirement comes before any transient calculation. For the lowest ripple, use low-ESR polymer, tantalum or organic-semiconductor parts; several capacitors in parallel close to the module are fine. The bank must carry a ripple current of at least 0.5 × ILR(P-P). More capacitance lowers ripple as long as ESR is low enough. One suggested bank is 220 µF, 7 mΩ specialty polymer with 100 µF, 6.3 V X5R ceramic, plus small ceramics for high-frequency EMI.

Little input capacitance is inside the module; the external capacitors, which may be several in parallel, sit very close to it and are sized mainly for ripple current. The suggested minimum is 22 µF X7R or X5R ceramic rated at least 25% above the highest input voltage, allowing for voltage and temperature derating. A higher-ESR bulk capacitor can damp resonance between the input capacitors and the supply wiring inductance; the typical application uses a 150 µF, 50 V aluminium part, often not needed.
The inductor inside the module is 3.3 µH; it mainly sets the inductor ripple current amplitude.

The supply should be well regulated, between 6 V and 20 V, able to deliver the peak input current, and of low enough resistance that an input current step does not pull VIN into a false UVLO trip. When the source sits several inches away or more, add bulk capacitance besides the ceramics; 47 µF or 100 µF electrolytic is typical and the value is not critical.

Keep the switched current loops small: put CIN1 right beside VIN and the PGND exposed pad, and ground the input and output capacitors to a local top-layer plane tied to the pad. Return the ground ends of the FB, SS and EN parts to AGND, with one connection from AGND (pin 4) to EP/PGND. Keep RFBT, RFBB and CFF near FB with a small copper area, routed away from the module body, since FB is high impedance. Make the input and output traces wide, and run a separate sense trace from the load to the feedback divider. Under the pad use a 6 × 10 array of thermal vias, 8 mil minimum diameter at 39 mil (1.0 mm) pitch, into the ground plane and inner planes, with enough copper to keep the junction below 125°C.

Work out dissipation using the average load current and the highest VIN, interpolating between the characteristic curves where needed, and keep the junction under 125°C. The board copper joined to the exposed pad is the heat sink; in the 12 V to 3.3 V, 5 A, 85°C example, about 67 cm² of 2 oz copper on each outer layer with about sixty 8 mil vias at 1.0 mm pitch is needed. The thermal derating curves hold for θJA = 12 °C/W.

Lands may be defined by the soldermask or not. Size the stencil for about 80% paste coverage of the exposed pad land and 1:1 for the other pads; stencil 0.125 mm to 0.15 mm thick. Use SAC alloy paste such as SAC 305, type 3 or finer. Set reflow to the paste supplier's profile for the board; only one reflow is allowed. Moisture sensitivity is level 3 at 245°C peak, 168 h.
Tested to EN 55022:2006 +A1:2007 and FCC Part 15 Subpart B:2007 Class B on the LMZ23605/03, LMZ22005/03 demonstration board at VIN = 12 V, VO = 3.3 V, IO = 5 A.
Pin compatible with LMZ23605, LMZ23603 and LMZ22003.
